forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 22%. No lab or government has declared AGI and there is no convergence of 3+ leading researchers on 'achieved'. Amodei keeps a ~2026-27 'powerful AI' framing and Hassabis stays ~50% by 2030; Metaculus community ~25% for AGI by 2029. Early-July capability news (model releases) does not touch the resolution bar. Unchanged.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: near-term insider predictions of a transformative technology arriving within a fixed ~3.5-year window, where insiders carry optimism incentives. Such forecasts resolve YES well under half the time; base ~15-20%.

factors_up.factor: Lab leadership timelines (Anthropic 'powerful AI' 2026-27; Altman 'within the term') sit inside the window
Metaculus community ~25% for AGI by 2029 and rapid frontier-model cadence (Claude Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 in 2026)

factors_down.factor: Resolution bar (clean credible declaration or 3+ researchers) remains unmet and definitionally contested
Hassabis and other cautious voices keep the field short of a shared 'achieved' call; Bulletin of Atomic Scientists notes timeline slippage

key_uncertainties: Whether any major lab will formally declare 'AGI' rather than avoiding the term
Whether 3+ leading researchers would publicly converge on 'AGI achieved' before 2030
update_triggers: Revise UP if a credible lab announces AGI or 3+ leading researchers state it is achieved
Revise DOWN if labs explicitly push timelines beyond 2030 or capability progress visibly stalls

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 26%. Early-July reporting reaffirms direction, not magnitude: McKinsey cutting ~3,000-4,000 roles (~10%), with Bain, BCG, Deloitte and KPMG (~400 US advisory) trimming or slowing hiring. But cuts stay concentrated in junior/back-office roles while AI/tech-enabled work grows (BCG projecting ~40% of revenue from AI in 2026, Bain ~30%). Firms are reshaping, not collapsing; no sector-wide ≥33% revenue or employment fall, ~4.5 years to run.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: professional-services sectors facing a major technology shock rarely contract ≥33% in headline value/employment within ~6 years; historically closer to 10-20% even in severe disruptions. Base ~15-20%.

factors_up.factor: McKinsey down ~10% and peers cutting/freezing junior hiring, explicitly citing AI productivity
Entry-level 'pyramid' economics eroding as GenAI compresses research/analyst workflows

factors_down.factor: ≥33% decline in revenue OR employment attributed primarily to AI is a very high, specific bar
Firms reallocating rather than shrinking (BCG growing AI/tech headcount); senior/specialist demand robust

key_uncertainties: Whether headcount cuts deepen into a sector-wide ≥33% contraction vs. plateau at ~10-15%
Whether 2+ credible analyses would attribute any decline *primarily* to AI rather than macro/cyclical factors
update_triggers: Revise UP if MBB/Big-Four announce further large AI-attributed cuts or revenue falls materially
Revise DOWN if consulting revenue/headcount stabilises or rebounds through 2027

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 6%. PollCheck 7-poll average (4 Jul) has Reform 25.7%, Labour 21.4%, Conservatives 19.0%. Labour sits a clear second, ~4pts behind Reform, with the election not due until 2029. Recovery to 'largest party' remains possible over that horizon but is currently an underdog scenario.
forecasts.base_rate: Governing parties trailing by ~5pts mid-term sometimes recover to plurality by polling day, but a fragmented five-party field and a sustained Reform lead lower the odds; base ~15-20% for the incumbent, discounted here.

factors_up.factor: Election ~3+ years away; incumbency, fiscal levers and FPTP vote distribution can still favour Labour
Labour still leads in London and holds an efficient seat geography vs. a spread Reform vote

factors_down.factor: Sustained Reform lead since 2025 with Labour support 'fallen considerably'
Five-way vote split makes a Labour plurality of seats harder to reconstruct

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform's lead proves durable or narrows as an election approaches
How FPTP converts a fragmented vote into seats
update_triggers: Revise UP if Labour recovers a polling lead or Reform fragments
Revise DOWN if Reform's lead widens or an early election is called with Labour behind

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 83%. A ~10-year window captures most credible insider and community timelines (Legg ~50% by 2028; Hassabis ~50% by 2030), leaving high but not near-certain probability. No early-July development changes the trajectory; capability cadence stays strong while formal 'declaration' risk persists.
forecasts.base_rate: Aggregating expert and market forecasts, most place >50% cumulative probability on AGI by the early-mid 2030s; a decade-long window pushes the central estimate well above half.

factors_up.factor: Multiple leading researchers put 50% odds by 2028-2030, comfortably inside 2035
Sustained scaling, agentic capability gains and heavy capex

factors_down.factor: Definitional/declaration risk: capability could arrive without a clean, agreed 'AGI achieved' call
Possible scaling plateau or unforeseen technical bottlenecks over the decade

key_uncertainties: Whether progress sustains or hits a wall before 2035
Whether resolution criteria (declaration / 3+ researchers) are cleanly satisfied
update_triggers: Revise UP on a formal AGI declaration or clear researcher consensus
Revise DOWN if scaling stalls or timelines slip past 2035

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 7%. AEI's 2 July update reiterates a 2026 blockade/invasion is unlikely and that Beijing prefers grey-zone coercion; the PLA maintains a near-permanent paramilitary presence and Taiwan is running July supply-chain/anti-blockade drills. These are coercion, not the >72hr blockade or assault the question requires. 2027 remains a capability milestone, keeping non-trivial tail risk through 2029.
forecasts.base_rate: Great-power initiation of a major blockade/invasion in any given ~3.5-year window is historically rare; base low single digits to low teens.

factors_up.factor: 2027 PLA readiness milestone falls inside the window; rising warship presence and carrier operations
Structural pressure on Xi's Taiwan timeline and continued erosion of the status quo

factors_down.factor: Analysts judge 2026 unlikely; invasion assessed as extremely costly for the PRC
Beijing's revealed preference for coercion short of the resolution threshold

key_uncertainties: Whether a 2027 capability milestone translates into intent this decade
Whether a grey-zone action escalates into a formal >72hr blockade
update_triggers: Revise UP on mobilisation signs, a declared quarantine/blockade, or a cross-strait crisis
Revise DOWN on cross-strait de-escalation or credible restraint signals

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 2%. Latest ONS print (May 2026, released 17 Jun) has CPI at 2.8%, unchanged for a second month, with core 2.6% and services 3.7% — inflation is sticky and well above target. Only ~7 monthly readings remain before the Jan 2027 deadline (June out 22 Jul); a sub-2.0% month would require an abrupt, unforecast fall. Very unlikely.
forecasts.base_rate: Conditional on CPI sitting at 2.8% with sticky services inflation, the chance any single month prints <2.0% within ~7 months is low; base a few percent.

factors_up.factor: Base effects and any sharp energy/food disinflation could briefly undercut 2.0%

factors_down.factor: CPI stuck at 2.8% two months running; services 3.7% and core rising
Few readings left before the deadline leave little room for a large, fast fall

key_uncertainties: Whether an energy-price base effect produces a one-month dip
update_triggers: Revise UP if a monthly CPI print drops sharply toward or below 2.0%
Revise DOWN as remaining months elapse above 2.0%

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 93%. Film opens 31 July 2026 with the best US first-day presales in ~5 years (past $40M) and domestic opening tracking ~$228-250M, despite losing opening-weekend IMAX screens to The Odyssey. ~5 months of run before the deadline. $1.5B is a top-tier bar only a handful of films clear, but record franchise demand keeps this high-probability.
forecasts.base_rate: Among the strongest-tracking tentpoles with a beloved franchise lead, a majority clear $1.5B lifetime; conditioning on record presales lifts the estimate high.

factors_up.factor: Record US first-day presales and ~$200M opening projection
Prior Holland Spider-Man film (No Way Home) cleared ~$1.9B; strong China/global franchise pull

factors_down.factor: $1.5B is a rare threshold; sharp second-week drops or weak legs could fall short
Execution/reception risk and competitive Q4 corridor

update_triggers: Revise UP on a record opening weekend and strong holds
Revise DOWN on a soft opening or steep second-weekend drop

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 99%. Mid-2026 reporting has Anthropic at a ~$30-47B run-rate (OpenAI disputes ~$8B of the gross figure) and OpenAI ~$25-33B; combined ARR is already at or above the $70B bar even on conservative net accounting, and both are compounding fast. Q4 2026 clearing $70B is near-certain barring a shock.
forecasts.base_rate: Given a combined ~$50-55B run-rate mid-year and steep growth, reaching >$70B by Q4 is the overwhelmingly likely path.

factors_up.factor: Combined run-rate already ~$50-55B with rapid sequential growth
Enterprise + coding demand (Claude Code) and ChatGPT scale sustaining momentum

factors_down.factor: Accounting disputes (OpenAI says Anthropic overstates by ~$8B) could affect which figure is 'credible'
Tail risk of a demand shock or reporting gap by Q4

key_uncertainties: Which ARR definition credible outlets use at Q4
Any abrupt slowdown (unlikely on current trajectory)
update_triggers: Revise DOWN only on a sharp, documented revenue reversal
Confirm on Q4 Bloomberg/The Information/FT ARR reporting

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 38%. OBR (March 2026) has 2026 GDP at 1.1%, averaging ~1.6% across 2027-30 as potential productivity rises toward ~1%, but the IFS is more pessimistic (TFP only ~0.4% by 2030). A 10-year >1.5% headline average is plausible if the productivity/AI lift materialises but is not the central path; roughly a third-to-40% chance.
forecasts.base_rate: UK trend growth has averaged ~1.3-1.5% since the mid-2000s; clearing a 1.5% decadal average requires above-trend productivity, so a sub-50% prior is appropriate.

factors_up.factor: OBR assumes productivity recovers toward ~1%+ and AI adds ~0.2pp by horizon
Long lookahead allows structural/AI upside to compound across the decade

factors_down.factor: Population ageing and lower net migration drag on labour-supply growth (~0.5% by 2030)
Persistent post-2008 UK productivity weakness; near-term growth ~1.1-1.6%

key_uncertainties: Whether the assumed productivity/AI pickup actually materialises
Net migration and labour-force trajectory through the 2030s
update_triggers: Revise UP on evidence of a durable productivity/AI acceleration
Revise DOWN on further productivity disappointment or migration-driven labour-supply weakness
